what: A capacity-aware chained-insertion score. It combines exact insertion distance, a mild far-from-depot credit, the cheapest feasible depot-relative continuation, a penalty for stranding nearby demand that no longer fits, and a quadratic unused-capacity penalty when the insertion would close the route. Cost per call is O(len(route) + len(unassigned)) time and O(1) space.
why: The insertion delta chooses locally economical slots, while the radial credit helps the route absorb remote customers near its farthest seed instead of leaving expensive isolated trips. The continuation term promotes geographically coherent chains, and the capacity terms discourage fragmenting close demand or closing a route with substantial unusable capacity—important under the varied demand and capacity pressure shown in the representative instances. The weights are scale-compatible but heuristic: they are not a remaining-cost estimate, do not guarantee improvement, and may overvalue route utilization when geographically separate routes would be preferable.
